newsitem.title: USA: AGA unconcerned about U.S. natgas inventories.
newsitem.headline: AGA unconcerned about U.S. natgas inventories.

text.p: Although natural gas trading has been volatile over the last few days and temperatures colder than normal over the last 10 weeks, the American Gas Association is confident there will be no shortfall of natural gas this winter.
"We're confident that supplies will be adequate," Tom Fisher, chairman of AGA and CEO of NICOR Inc, said Tuesday.
While U.S. inventories are about 10 percent lower than last year, in the key New England area storage is 85 percent full, which AGA president Michael Baly said was about the same level as a year ago.
He said a drop in inventories in producing areas this year reflected producers' bids to avoid getting stuck with large stocks.
"In years past, producers have had too much left in storage," Baly said at a news conference.
Overall in 1996, natural gas well completions were expected to surpass oil well completions for the fourth straight year, he said.
Since January, the monthly average for natural gas rigs in operation has climbed from 406 to more than 480 at the end of last month.
